email_enabled.description: Says the instance sends email at all.

email_notifications.description: Says notifications also reach them by email (when the instance sends email).

sms_enabled.description: Says the instance sends text messages; Phone is their mobile number (empty when none), PhoneVerified that they confirmed it with the code texted to it, and SMSNotifications that notifications also reach them by SMS (only those whose template asks).

theme.description: How the web UI is drawn for them: auto (follow the device), light or dark.

AccountRequest.description: Changes the signed-in person's own preferences.

sms_notifications.description: Turns text messages on or off (once the number is verified).

class_label.description: The class's label; the class name itself when no installed app defines the class any more.

depth.description: How many relationships away it is.

via_id.description: And ViaName are the item it is reached through: one of those asked about when depth is 1.

ApiForm.description: How a record type's fields are laid out: every field the form places, which go on the form for filing one and in which sections on the record. Whether each is shown, required or writable right now is a ticket's field_states, or for a record being filed, POST /forms/{type}/states.

app.description: The app that defines the form; empty for the form a type has without one.

create.description: Lists the fields on the form for filing one, in order.

create_sections.description: Lays them out: each section's fields flow into as many columns as fit (up to three), or sit in the columns it gives.

detail.description: Lists the sections of fields shown on the record, in order. Title, description and priority have places of their own there and are not listed.

reactive.description: The fields the form's conditions read: when one of them changes while filing, ask for the states again.

ApiFormField.description: One field: one of the record's own (core) or an extra field the form declares.

core.description: Set for the record's own fields, which requests name directly (title, resolution) or under change; extra fields go under fields.

default.description: What a new record starts with, for extra fields that have one.

required.description: Set when the field is always required; field_states says when it is now.

type.description: Text, textarea, number, boolean, date, datetime or choice; the core priority field is priority.

ApiKeptPerson.description: Someone this instance keeps when a clone replaces its people.

ApiKey.description: An API key as it is listed: never the key itself.

prefix.description: The key's first characters (slk_ and eight more), to tell keys apart.

rate_limit.description: The key's own limit, requests a minute (0: none); null follows the setting for keys.

scopes.description: The permissions the key is narrowed to; absent when it may do everything its account may.

rate_limit.description: The key's own limit, requests a minute: 0 for none, 10 to 1,000,000, or null to follow the setting for keys (Admin → Rate limits).

Approval.description: One pending approval request, with enough of the ticket to show in a list. Anyone can be asked to approve something, staff or not, so this is not a staff-only endpoint.

group.description: The group the person is asked to decide for, when they are asked as one of its members: the first of them to answer decides for the group.

audience.description: Everyone (anyone signed in) or internal (staff, with knowledge:read_internal).

body.description: Markdown, as written. Render it with a sanitiser: it is never HTML to trust.

moves.description: The status changes the reader may make now (single-article responses).

tickets.description: The records linked to it that the reader may see (single-article responses, for staff).

version.description: Counts the saves of its content, from 1.

ArticleHit.description: An article in a list or search result.

snippet.description: A piece of the body: around the matches when searching, the start otherwise. Matches are between U+2E22 and U+2E23; it is plain text, never HTML.

ArticleRef.description: An article linked to a record.

ArticleRequest.description: An article's content as it is written or changed; on PATCH, a field left out keeps its value.

ArticleStatusRequest.description: Moves an article to another status.

to.description: Review (a writer sends a draft for review), draft (back to its writer), published or retired (those who publish).

ArticleTicket.description: A record an article is linked to.

ArticleVersion.description: One saved version of an article; the list leaves out the content.

Attachment.description: A file attached to a record.

attached_at.description: When the upload finished and the file joined the record (null while it uploads): where it sits among the record's comments.

can_delete.description: Says the reader may remove it: they added it, or may update the record.

inline.description: Says the file is a picture the browser may show (download with inline=true); anything else is saved.

status.description: Pending while the upload is in flight (only its uploader sees it), then ready.

folder.description: Where snapshots kept in a folder are, on the worker and api servers.

key_configured.description: Says whether this server has a secrets key: without one no snapshot can be taken or read.

key_id.description: The key snapshots are encrypted under now; a snapshot under another key needs that key to restore.

s3_configured.description: Says whether Admin → Storage has an S3 bucket, which the s3 destination needs.

schema_version.description: This server's, to compare a snapshot's with.

Calendar.description: A business calendar: the working hours an SLA counts, in a time zone, less holidays. An SLA definition names one by name.

created_by_name.description: Who added it; null for the built-in one or once that person is deleted.

hours.description: The working week: day 0 is Sunday, start and end are HH:MM (end may be 24:00).

name.description: What an SLA definition writes after calendar: (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens).

time_zone.description: An IANA zone such as Europe/London; hours and holidays are in it.

CalendarEntry.description: One record's planned window on the calendar.

change_type.description: And Risk are the change's own fields (standard, normal or emergency; low, medium, high or "").

freezes.description: The ids of the change freezes this window overlaps that apply to it: those for every change, and those limited to an item it is linked to (see freezes in the response).

overlaps.description: The references of the other entries whose windows overlap this one, counting only records still to be done (open or waiting): two changes in the same window are a conflict to look at.

prefix.description: The leading part of Reference (the type's prefix), for styling; show Reference as given.

CalendarRequest.description: A calendar as it is added or changed. On PATCH, a field left out keeps its value.

CatalogApp.description: An app new items can be added to, with the workflows an item of it may name.

CatalogEntry.description: An item in the editor's list: every item, whoever it is for.

available_to.description: Who may order it; absent, everyone.

edited.description: Says it was changed here; Shipped that its app (or a local file) defines it.

icon.description: One of a fixed set of pictures (laptop, software, access...).

CatalogItem.description: An item in the catalog, as the list shows it.

icon.description: One of a fixed set of pictures (laptop, software, access...).

CatalogItemDef.description: An item as the editor changes it: the same definition its file holds.

workflows.description: Its app's workflows for requests, any of which may fulfil it.

yaml.description: The item as a file; Override is the edit as it is kept (what `servicelater app export-local` writes).

CatalogItemDetail.description: An item with what ordering it needs.

can_order_for_others.description: Says the caller may name someone else as who it is for (records:update:request).

form.description: Its questions: fields, and which are asked when ordering (create) and shown on the request (detail).

icon.description: One of a fixed set of pictures (laptop, software, access...).

CatalogItemSaveRequest.description: An item as the editor saves it. App names the app a new item goes in (an existing item stays in its own).

CatalogStatesRequest.description: An order as far as it is filled in.

fields.description: The answers so far, by question name.

ChangeFields.description: A change's own fields in a request. Absent fields are left alone; planned_start and planned_end take null to clear them.

impact.description: Low, medium, high, or "" for not assessed.

planned_end.description: When the window closes, after the start.

risk.description: Low, medium, high, or "" for not assessed.

status.description: Queued, sent, failed or skipped; Detail says why, for the last three.

ChildRun.description: A run a subflow or foreach step started.

ChildTask.description: A record under another: one team's part of the work.

class_label.description: The class's label; the class name itself when no installed app defines the class any more.

fields.description: Its class's fields that have a value, by name.

relationships.description: Every relationship it is in, either way round (GET /cis/{id}, at most 500; null in the answer to a change).

support_group_id.description: The group that fixes it when it breaks.

tickets.description: The records linked to it that the reader may see, open ones first (GET /cis/{id}, at most 100; null in the answer to a change).

CiRelation.description: One relationship as seen from an item.

impact.description: Says trouble spreads along it (towards this item when outgoing, away from it otherwise).

label.description: How it reads from this item: the type's label when this item comes first, its reverse otherwise.

outgoing.description: Says this item comes first ("this depends on item").

CiRequest.description: An item as it is added or changed. On PATCH, a field left out keeps its value; owner_group_id and support_group_id take null to clear them, and fields sets the class's fields by name (null clears one).

CiSummary.description: An item as lists show it.

class_label.description: The class's label; the class name itself when no installed app defines the class any more.

CiTicket.description: A record linked to an item.

extends.description: The class it builds on; ancestors are every class it builds on, nearest first. Filtering items by a class finds those of the classes that extend it too.

fields.description: Its fields, those of the classes it extends first.

environment.description: This instance's; a production one refuses clones unless allow_into_production.

keep.description: The people a clone keeps (with whoever applies it).

source.description: Where this instance pulls packages from.

switched.description: The settings the last clone's safety switch turns off, as they are now.

CloneLoad.description: One package uploaded here, and what became of it.

origin.description: Upload or pull (fetched from the source; it needs no passphrase).

report.description: What the load brought and kept, once done.

scheduled_for.description: When the schedule asked for it, for a scheduled pull.

source.description: The package's header: the instance, environment and profile it came from, when, at which schema.

status.description: Pulling (being fetched from the source), uploaded (waiting to be applied), pending, running, done or failed (Error says why; a load that failed changed nothing). An uploaded one may carry an Error too: a scheduled pull that was fetched but not applied says why.

CloneLoadRequest.description: Previews or applies an uploaded package.

confirm.description: This instance's name (or "clone" when it has none), for applying.

keep_people.description: Keeps the people on the keep list (whoever applies it is kept either way).

keep_studio.description: Keeps this instance's workflow, form and catalog edits over production's.

passphrase.description: The one the package was made with (left out for a package pulled from the source).

report.description: What it holds and what it left out, once ready.

status.description: Pending, running, ready or failed (Error says why).

destination.description: Folder or s3 (the bucket of Admin → Storage, under clones/).

passphrase.description: Encrypts the package (at least 12 characters): the target asks for it when the package is loaded. It is kept, sealed under the secrets key, only until the package is made.

name.description: Short (uat, dev-small): lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

CloneSource.description: The clone source: its address, the schedule, and whether a pull key is set (it is never shown).

CloneSourceRequest.description: Sets where this instance pulls clones from, and when.

confirm.description: This instance's name (or "clone" when it has none): needed to turn the schedule on, or to change the address while it is on, since every scheduled pull replaces this instance's records without asking again.

key.description: The source's pull key (Admin → Clones → a profile → Pull keys there); left out or empty, the one set stays. Setting it needs settings:manage too, as every secret does.

CloneSourceTest.description: What a source said about itself.

warnings.description: What may stop its packages loading here, or should make someone look twice.

CloneSourceTestRequest.description: Tries a source, the one set or another.

url.description: And Key, when given, are tried instead of the ones set.

CloneType.description: A record type a profile can choose.

folder.description: Where packages kept in a folder are.

key_configured.description: Says whether this server has a secrets key, which holds a package's passphrase until it is made.

masked_fields.description: The form fields marked mask: true, which masking fields leaves out.

pull_keys.description: The profiles' pull keys, revoked ones too; Pulls the latest pulls other instances made.

record_types.description: The types a profile can take.

s3_configured.description: Says whether Admin → Storage has an S3 bucket, which the s3 destination needs.

CmdbModel.description: What configuration items can be: the installed classes, how items can relate, and the statuses every item has. All of it comes from apps except the statuses.

on_behalf_of_name.description: Names the person an app acted for, when an app wrote the comment (author_name is then the app).

parts.description: Every part, in order, with the ETag storage answered for it.

hosts.description: The hosts its http.request steps may call (*.example.com: its subdomains).

set.description: Says a value is stored (encrypted); UpdatedAt and UpdatedBy when, and by whom.

ConnectionSecretRequest.description: A secret's new value; null clears it.

CoreField.description: One of a type's own fields, which a form may relabel, explain, lay out and set conditions on.

on_create.description: Says it may be asked when filing; Detail that it may be laid out on the record.

content_type.description: The file's media type, as the browser reports it.

filename.description: The file's name, as it will be shown and saved; any folder part is dropped.

size.description: The file's size in bytes, at most the instance's max_size.

kind.description: Notification or test; What says which notification (a template, or approval_pending).

status.description: Queued, sent, failed or skipped; Detail says why it failed or was skipped.

user_name.description: Who it was for, when it was for someone.

Download.description: Where to fetch a file: a short-lived URL that needs no sign-in, to open or link to.

expires_at.description: When the URL stops working (a download already started carries on).

EmailSettings.description: How this instance sends email. The password is never sent back: only whether it is set.

key_configured.description: Says the server has a secrets key (SL_SECRETS_KEY or SL_SECRETS_KEY_FILE); without one the password cannot be set.

password_readable.description: False when the password was stored with a key this server does not have, so it must be set again.

password_set.description: Says the mail server password is stored (encrypted); PasswordUpdatedAt and PasswordUpdatedBy say when and by whom it was last set.

EmailSettingsRequest.description: Replaces the email settings. password sets the mail server password, null clears it, and leaving it out keeps it.

Error.description: Every failure has this shape. The message is meant for a person.

FormDef.description: A form as the editor changes it: the definition its file holds, and what the editor needs around it.

app.description: The app the form is (or an edit would be) kept in.

values.description: Counts the records holding a value for each extra field, by name, including fields the form no longer has: a field with values keeps its name and type.

yaml.description: The form as a file; Override the edit as it is kept (what `servicelater app export-local` writes).

FormEntry.description: A record type in the editor's list.

app.description: The app whose form it is, or that an edit goes in (the type's owner when it has no form).

builtin.description: Says no app gives the type a form: it has the one made of its own fields.

catalog.description: Says its forms are its catalog items' questions, edited in the catalog editor.

extra_fields.description: Counts the fields the form adds.

FormSaveRequest.description: A form as the editor saves it.

FormStates.description: How the form for filing stands for a draft.

values.description: What the before rules would set fields to, by name, where that differs from the draft.

FormStatesRequest.description: A record being filed, as far as it is filled in.

fields.description: The extra fields filled in so far, by name.

Freeze.description: A change freeze: a period when changes may not be scheduled. What a freeze stops is up to the apps installed (change-management refuses a planned window that overlaps one, except for an emergency change, and holds back work that would start during one).

created_by_name.description: Who declared it; null once that person is deleted.

item_ids.description: The configuration items it is limited to; empty means it applies to every change. Items are those of them the reader may see (with cmdb:read), with their names.

FreezeRequest.description: A freeze as it is declared or changed. On PATCH, a field left out keeps its value.

items.description: Limits it to changes linked to one of these configuration items, by id; [] (or leaving it out on create) makes it apply to every change. Needs cmdb:read.

Grant.description: A role given to a person or to a group (everyone in it).

user_id.description: Set for a grant to a person, GroupID for one to a group.

GraphEdge.description: One way out of a step. Kind is empty for the ordinary "next", and "then"/"else"/"timeout" for the branches a condition, wait or approval step can take, so the viewer can label them.

Group.description: A team: what a ticket is routed to, and what group('name') in a workflow resolves to.

calendar_id.description: The business calendar the group works by, or null: SLAs that count "the assignment group's calendar" use it for records routed here.

name.description: Unique whatever its case; expressions refer to a group by it.

restricted.description: Keeps the records routed to it to its members (and their requesters, assignees and those who hold restricted:read): other staff do not see them.

GroupDetail.description: A group with everyone in it, and the roles it gives them.

calendar_id.description: The business calendar the group works by, or null: SLAs that count "the assignment group's calendar" use it for records routed here.

name.description: Unique whatever its case; expressions refer to a group by it.

restricted.description: Keeps the records routed to it to its members (and their requesters, assignees and those who hold restricted:read): other staff do not see them.

GroupRef.description: Names a group someone is in.

HeldRole.description: A role someone or a group holds, and through what.

grant_id.description: The grant to revoke to take it away.

group_id.description: And GroupName say which group a person holds it through; empty when it was granted to them.

HistoryEntry.description: One thing that happened to a record or an item. Values are given as stored (old, new) and as people read them (old_text, new_text: names rather than ids, labels rather than codes), resolved for the reader: something they may not see reads as "an item" or "a record".

action.description: Created, changed, linked, unlinked or deleted.

actor_name.description: Who did it; ActorApp is set when an app did, for OnBehalfOfName. Both are empty for ServiceLater itself (the SLA timer, say).

field.description: What changed as stored (status, fields.category, ci...); Label is what people call it.

kind.description: Says how to show the values: text, time (RFC 3339, for the reader's time zone) or long (show the before and after rather than inline).

old_text.description: And NewText are the values as people read them.

HistoryExclusion.description: A field an app leaves out of history.

subject.description: Task (a record type, Kind) or ci (a class, Kind).

HistorySettings.description: What is recorded field by field. The basics are always recorded whatever it says: a record's creation, status, assignee and assignment group, and an item's creation, status and deletion.

exclusions.description: The fields apps leave out of history (history: false in a form or a class).

log.description: Who changed these settings and when, newest first, so a gap in history can be told from a quiet record.

record_type_options.description: The record types in use, to choose from.

Impact.description: What trouble with some items reaches.

truncated.description: Says the walk stopped early (more than 10 relationships away, or more than 1000 items).

ImportReport.description: The result of reading an import file, and of applying it when asked.

applied.description: Says the changes were made; otherwise this is a preview, or the import was refused for its problems.

ImportRow.description: What an import does, or would do, with one row of the file.

class.description: The item's class, for a file that covers a class and those extending it.

id.description: The item created or updated (for an item row once applied, or one already there).

problem.description: Says why the row cannot be imported.

row.description: The line of the file the row is on (the header is line 1).

reference.description: And Title are the record it is on, when the reader may see it.

action.description: Comment, incident, ignored, refused or failed; Detail says why.

reference.description: The record it was added to or filed as.

password_set.description: SecretSet says the IMAP password, or the Graph client secret (by mode), is stored (encrypted; never shown).

Limits.description: The rate limits and what they would be if nobody had changed them.

defaults.description: The limits as shipped, for the page to show beside each one.

MadePullKey.description: A new pull key, with the key itself.

key.description: The key itself, shown only in this response: enter it on the target, in Admin → Clone in → Source.

prefix.description: The key's first characters (slp_ and eight more), to tell keys apart.

deactivated_at.description: Set for someone who can no longer sign in. They stay listed, but group() leaves them out.

Move.description: One thing a person may try to do to a ticket right now. The server decides what is offered, so clients never hold a copy of the lifecycle's rules: they show these, and say why one is blocked.

blocked.description: why it is not available at the moment

Notification.description: One hint that something needs this person's attention. The stored row names what happened and which record; the text is filled in now, from the record as this person may see it, so a notification never carries more than its recipient could read for themselves.

body.description: More detail, when the template has any.

kind.description: Approval_pending (a workflow asks this person to decide) or template (an app's notify rule).

link.description: Where the notification leads in the web app.

reference.description: That ticket's reference, such as INC42.

task_id.description: The ticket a template notification is about.

description.description: Anything else the requester wants to say, when the item asks (its form places description).

fields.description: The answers to the item's questions, by name.

requester_id.description: Orders it for someone else (needs records:update:request); the caller by default.

PartReceipt.description: What storage answered for a part.

PartURL.description: Where to PUT one part: the URL (absolute when it goes straight to the bucket), and how many bytes.

PartURLsRequest.description: Asks where to send some of an upload's parts.

numbers.description: The parts (from 1), at most 100 at a time.

deactivated_at.description: Set when an admin deactivated them: they cannot sign in, and pickers leave them out.

manager_id.description: Their manager, who approves what they request (record.requester_manager_id in workflows).

service_account.description: Set for an integration's account: it cannot sign in, and calls the API with API keys.

PullKey.description: One of a profile's pull keys (the key itself is shown only when it is made).

prefix.description: The key's first characters (slp_ and eight more), to tell keys apart.

chart.description: How the workbench draws the view's columns; null or absent: a table.

shared.description: Makes it readable by everyone who may run queries (each still sees only their own rows).

sql.description: One SELECT over the query views and other saved views, with no parameters ($1...).

QueryRun.description: One query the caller ran, or tried to.

outcome.description: Ok, refused, failed or timeout; Error says why when it is not ok.

saved_views.description: The saved views the caller may read, read by name like the built-in ones.

views.description: The built-in views, with what each column holds.

QueueCounts.description: How many records each view of the queue holds for the caller.

due.description: Due: open work with an SLA clock running or breached, which the Due view lists first.

groups.description: Groups: open work routed to a group the caller is in.

mine.description: Mine: open work assigned to the caller.

open.description: Open: all open and waiting work the caller may see.

unassigned.description: Unassigned: open work nobody has taken.

RecordType.description: A record type in use: an installed app defines its lifecycle.

app.description: The app that defines the type; empty for a core type.

can_file.description: Says whether the caller may file one as themselves: the type is open to everyone, or they have records:create:<type>.

can_file_for_others.description: Says whether they may also name someone else as the requester (records:update:<type> too).

description.description: Says what the type is for; empty for most core types.

from_catalog.description: Types (requests) are ordered from the service catalog; CanFile says whether the caller may also file one by hand, with no item.

plural.description: What a list of them is called (Incidents, Things).

RelationRequest.description: Relates an item to another: {"type", "to"} reads "this <type> to", {"type", "from"} reads "from <type> this". Give exactly one of to and from.

Relationship.description: A way items can relate: label reads from the first item to the second ("depends on"), reverse from the second to the first ("used by"). With impact, trouble with the second item affects the first.

Restore.description: One restore, asked for or done.

status.description: Pending, running, done or failed (Error says why; a failed restore changed nothing).

change_schema.description: Allows a snapshot from an older version: the database is migrated to it, loaded and migrated up.

confirm.description: Must be the instance's name (or "restore" when it has none): a restore replaces everything.

Role.description: A named set of permissions: a built-in base role, or one an app defines in roles/.

app.description: The app that defines the role; empty for the built-in base roles.

built_in.description: Roles are base roles: set on a person, never granted.

grants.description: How many people and groups the role is granted to.

RoleDetail.description: A role and who has it.

app.description: The app that defines the role; empty for the built-in base roles.

built_in.description: Roles are base roles: set on a person, never granted.

grants.description: How many people and groups the role is granted to.

Run.description: A workflow execution as the run viewer shows it.

parent_id.description: The run whose subflow or foreach step started this one; Children the runs this one's steps started.

start.description: Only on a single run: what the workflow looked like when it started, the variables now, and what happened.

params.description: The values of $1, $2, ... in order, as text; Postgres converts them to the types the query needs.

sql.description: One SELECT over the query views.

chart.description: How the workbench draws it; null shows a table.

columns.description: What it gives, worked out when it was saved.

mine.description: True when the caller owns it, and so may change it.

shared.description: Views can be read by everyone who may run queries; the rest only by their owner.

sql.description: Its query: one SELECT over the query views and other saved views, with no parameters.

uses.description: The saved views it reads directly.

app.description: The app the script belongs to: its script files are what the script may load.

file.description: File, when set, says this is that script file of the app rather than an inline script.

ScriptFile.description: A script file in an app.

edited.description: Says it was changed here; Shipped that its app (or a local file) has it.

used_by.description: The app's workflows and rules that load it (workflow:name, rule:name).

ScriptProblem.description: A mistake in a script, at a line (0: not about one line).

file.description: And FileLine are where in a script file the script loaded it went wrong.

changes.description: And Comments are what it asked for, in order: nothing was changed.

ok.description: False when the script failed (Problem) or stopped itself with abort (Aborted).

ScriptTestRequest.description: A script to try against a record.

app.description: The app the script belongs to: its script files are what the script may load.

record.description: The reference (INC42) or id of the record to run it for; leave it out for a workflow with none.

vars.description: A workflow's variables as the script would see them.

where.description: Workflow (the default), before or async: what the script may do, and its limits, follow from it.

mode.description: Says how the query was read: reference when it began with a record type's prefix (INC, INC42) and that found something, else text (the words, typos allowed).

prefix.description: The reference prefix the query began with, in reference mode.

SearchResult.description: One thing a search found, ready to show and to open.

detail.description: The small print beside it: a record's type and status, an item's class, a person's email.

link.description: The page in the web UI that shows it.

match.description: Says where a record matched when it was not its title: the field's label and the passage ("Serial number: SN-4412", "Description: …the VPN drops after…").

reference.description: How people name it (INC42, KB7); empty for items and people.

ServedPull.description: One pull another instance made from this one.

status.description: Running, done or failed (Error says why).

passwords.description: Who may sign in with a password: everyone, or admins only (the rest use single sign-on).

providers.description: The single sign-on buttons, in order.

SlaCalendarRequest.description: How an SLA chooses its hours.

calendar.description: The rules, in order: when (a condition on the record; empty always holds) and use (a calendar's name, 24x7 or group). The last should hold always, so every record gets hours.

SlaDef.description: An SLA and the hours it counts.

calendar.description: The label of the hours it counts by, "Every hour" when every hour counts.

secret_set.description: Says a client secret is stored (it is never shown).

visits.description: Visits, Failed and Timeouts count the visits of runs started in the window: all of them, the ones that failed the run there, and the waits that ran out.

key_configured.description: Says the server has a secrets key; without one the secret access key cannot be set.

offset.description: How many matching rows to skip.

delivery_key.description: The value of the webhook's dedupe header, when the call had one.

outcome.description: Started, duplicate (an earlier call with the same key started the run) or refused.

reason.description: Says why a call was refused.

remote.description: The address the call came from, as the server saw it.

run_id.description: The run it started or repeated; null when refused.

duplicate.description: True when an earlier call with the same dedupe header started RunID, and this one started nothing.

run_id.description: The workflow run the call started (GET /api/v1/workflow-runs/{id}, for those who may read runs).

edited.description: Says it was changed in ServiceLater's workflow builder.

in_flight.description: The runs still going, oldest first (at most 100); More says there are more.

runs.description: Counts the runs started in the window by how they stand: done, failed, cancelled, or still going.

steps.description: By step id. A run started on an older version may be at a step this one no longer has.

WorkflowApp.description: An installed app a workflow can belong to, and what its steps may then do.

WorkflowDef.description: A workflow as the builder edits it: the same definition its YAML file holds.

app_permissions.description: What the app may do (its manifest's permissions): a workflow's steps act as the app, for whoever started it, so a step needs one of these to read or change a record.

app_workflows.description: The app's workflows (what subflow and foreach may run); AppSecrets the secrets and AppHosts the hosts its http.request steps may use.

edited.description: Says it was changed in ServiceLater (the app's studio layer); Shipped that the app itself defines it, so resetting an edited one goes back to the app's version rather than removing it.

layers.description: Where the definition comes from: default, local, instance (files on the server) and studio.

layout.description: Where each step sits in the diagram; steps without a place are laid out from the graph.

override.description: The edit as it is kept (only what it changes, over the app's version): what `servicelater app export-local` writes, as the app's local/ file.

schedule.description: Starts it by the clock, if it has one.

steps.description: In the order they are written; which fields a step has depends on its type (see the workflow docs).

webhook.description: Starts it when another system calls POST /api/v1/hooks/{app}/{name}, if it has one.

webhook_secret_set.description: Says whether the webhook's secret has been set (Admin → Connections); until it is, every call is refused.

yaml.description: The definition as a file, for those who keep apps in version control.

WorkflowSaveRequest.description: A workflow as the builder saves it.

schedule.description: Starts it by the clock: cron, timezone and, to run once per record, for_each.

webhook.description: Starts it when another system calls it: secret, auth (token or hmac) and header names.

bearerAuth.description: An API key (slk_...) of a service account.

info.description:
Generated from the Go source of internal/api by `make openapi`; do not edit by hand.

Sign in with `POST /api/v1/auth/login`. It sets an `sl_access` cookie (a short-lived token) and an `sl_refresh` cookie; `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` renews both. Unsafe requests from a browser must come from the same origin.

Integrations use an API key instead: an admin makes a service account and a key for it (`POST /api/v1/service-accounts`, `POST /api/v1/users/{id}/api-keys`), and every request sends `Authorization: Bearer slk_...`. A key acts as its service account, narrowed to its scopes if it has any.

Permissions are checked twice: by role in the API, and by row-level security in the database, so a record you may not see answers 404, exactly like one that does not exist.

Live updates are a WebSocket at `/ws/v1/subscribe`, which is not described here: it sends hints with ids only, and clients refetch through this API.

get.description:
(cmdb:read): a class's items, and those of the classes extending it, as a CSV file, one per row, in the format an import reads; with template=true, the header row only. When other classes extend it, a class column says which class each row is, and the columns are every field of the family.

Requires the `cmdb:read` permission.

post.description:
(cmdb:manage) with a CSV file as the body: import items of a class and of the classes extending it. A row's class is its class cell (a name or label in the family; empty is the file's class). Each row is matched to an item of its class by name (case aside): a new name adds an item, a known one updates it, and an empty cell leaves that value as it is (an import never clears a value, removes an item or moves one to another class). A new name that another class of the family already has is a problem, not a second item: set the class to update that one. Groups are named; field cells take what the class's fields take, or a choice's label. Without apply=true nothing is written: the answer says what each row would do. With it, the import happens in one transaction, and only if no row has a problem (422 with the report otherwise), unless skip_errors=true, which imports the other rows.

Requires the `cmdb:manage` permission.

get.description:
(cmdb:read): every relationship between items as a CSV file, in the format an import reads (from_class, from_name, type, to_class, to_name); with template=true, the header row only.

Requires the `cmdb:read` permission.

post.description:
(cmdb:manage) with a CSV file as the body: relate items, one relationship per row, reading "from <type> to". Items are named by class (name or label) and name, and must exist already (import the items first); the type is its name or how it reads ("depends on"). A relationship already there is left alone; an import never removes one. apply and skip_errors work as for items.

Requires the `cmdb:manage` permission.

get.description:
(cmdb:read): the classes items can be, how they can relate, and their statuses.

Requires the `cmdb:read` permission.

Fields taken off keep their values in the records that have them; a field with values keeps its type.

Requires the `forms:manage` permission.

(workflows:read_all or workflows:edit): where the workflow's runs are right now, and how each step went for the runs started in the last 7 days, for the builder to show on its diagram. It changes as runs move: the run.changed event says when to ask again.

Requires the `workflows:read_all` or `workflows:edit` permission.

delete.description:
(workflows:edit): undo the edits made here: a workflow the app ships goes back to the app's version; one created here is removed. Runs in progress keep the version they started with.

Requires the `workflows:edit` permission.
